charlie (Customer): Hey folks — we started seeing short bursts of 429s this morning even though our overall quota looks fine. Happening for ~10-20s every 5m. Any ideas?

alex (Support): Sorry you're hitting that. Can you confirm if this is on Hosted or Dedicated? Also, do you have a timeline or sample request ids?

charlie (Customer): Hosted API, eu-west. Sample request ids: req_ablc1, req_ablc4. I pulled a quick timeline: 10:03:20 200, 10:03:25 429, 10:03:30 200, 10:03:35 429 — pattern repeats a few times.

maria (SRE): That pattern looks like burst-credit exhaustion + rapid refill window interactions (fractional refill). Are you using a high short-lived concurrency?

charlie (Customer): We run a cron that spikes 120 concurrent requests for ~15s every 5m to warm caches. Steady state is ~5 rps otherwise.

alex (Support): Yep that matches a microburst case. Our Burst Cushion (burst credits) smooths over short spikes but if the spike pattern drains then refills partially, you can see intermittent 429s as the pool oscillates.

sam (Eng): Quick repro commands if you want to simulate locally:
```
for i in {1..120}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-small","input":"warm"}' &
done; wait
```
This will create a ~15s microburst similar to your cron.

charlie (Customer): Nice — we'll try that. Any config on our side to avoid the flapping?

maria (SRE): Options: reduce concurrency of the warm job; add exponential backoff + jitter on 429s; request a higher base cushion from Support for that account; or move warm traffic to a dedicated route with reserved capacity.

alex (Support): Also note smoothing policy details: default window is 60s with fractional refill tick every 10s (approx). If your spike pattern is aligned with the refill ticks you can get alternating success/fail.

charlie (Customer): Is there a way to change the smoothing window or refill tick?

maria (SRE): Not tunable per-customer in Hosted right now. We tune globally to balance fairness. For immediate relief: stagger the cron (spread 120 into 6 waves of 20 with 2s gap) or drop concurrency to 60. We'll also open a temporary cushion bump from Support if you want.

alex (Support): I'll start the cushion request — can you confirm account id and desired cushion (e.g., +50 concurrent burst credits)?

charlie (Customer): Account ac-84321. Let's try +40 first. We'll also implement jittered retries.

sam (Eng): FYI: once you add retries, please implement capped retries and backoff: e.g., initial 200ms jittered, max 2s, 3 retries. Pattern: 200ms * 2^n + uniform(0,200ms).

quota-bot: [automated] Burst cushion request submitted: ac-84321 +40 credits; estimated SLA change window 1–2 business days. Ticket #SUP-7921.

alex (Support): Ticket created. We'll monitor the next few cron runs. If you still see flapping after cushion, ping here and we can look at route-level traces. :thumbsup:
